gap: No result ChatGPT got states that OutdoorGearLab (Kenji Mowrey, 2026-07-23) timed the EcoFlow DELTA 3 at a full 0–100 % wall charge in 50 minutes at an average 1,299 Wh/hr, with no app fast mode mentioned, while the same lab timed the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 at 56 minutes in its default mode.
standout_why: I compared against the cited OutdoorGearLab best-of page (updated 2026-07-23), the cited thisWATT guide, the cited Tested Watts charge-time page and our own current page. The OutdoorGearLab best-of page already lists the DELTA 3 at 0.8–0.9 hr and 1,229 Wh/hr, so rivals have part of this. It does not give the 50-minute figure, does not say that this beat EcoFlow's 56-minute claim, and does not put it next to the Anker's 56-minute default-mode time from the same lab. thisWATT says outright that it has done no testing ('We haven't tested these units hands-on'). Tested Watts gives only maker claims. Our page says the DELTA 3 was 'not measured by a major reviewer', and that is now wrong. In all seven ChatGPT answers the DELTA 3 shows as '56 min claimed'. None of the rival pages gives the energy a unit draws from the wall for a full charge. StorageReview's 1.18 kWh for the DELTA 3 Plus appears in none of them.
decides: This confirms the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 as the fastest pick. Two named reviewers each measured 47 minutes with UltraFast on: The Technology Man at about 20 °C, and The Solar Lab. It also sets up a clear second choice for shoppers who won't switch on an app mode. In OutdoorGearLab's single lab, the DELTA 3 filled in 50 minutes on its default charger, which beats the Anker's 56-minute default run there. So the Anker is only fastest with UltraFast enabled. The DJI Power 1000 V2 is borderline: The Technology Man measured under 53 minutes and OutdoorGearLab measured 59 minutes. The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 fails the under-an-hour test in OutdoorGearLab's run (almost 2 hours at 563 Wh/hr, mode not stated).

findings.label: Measured full wall charge, 0–100 % (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.note: Text: 'Taking just 50 minutes to complete a full charge with an average charge rate of 1,299 Wh/hr… even faster than EcoFlow's own advertised time of 56 minutes.' The same page's spec table says 0.9 hr and 1,229 Wh/hr, so the page contradicts itself. Charging mode and mains voltage are not stated. OutdoorGearLab is a US lab, but the voltage is not printed.
